subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - Competitive bake-off plan and next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Chen <samantha@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood competitive eval - post-call recap and ask

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo today — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and the asks we agreed on: 

- Goal: Validate inference cost and latency at our 5k QPS-equivalent batch mix and ensure output parity vs our current hyperscaler provider (CloudCorp).
- Primary tests: latency p50/p95, token cost per 1M tokens, quality regression on our 10-prod prompts for routing/QA.
- Timeline: We would like a 2-week bake-off window starting next week if possible.

Next steps we discussed: 
1) Redwood to share a proposed bake-off plan and success criteria (owners, test harness, datasets).
2) Acme to provide a 10-prompt goldset + a small representative dataset and an account with access tokens for CloudCorp endpoints.
3) Schedule a 30–45m sync next Tue to kick off and confirm infra + metrics.

Files: I attached a short doc (sample-goldset.csv) showing prompt categories.

Questions: is it reasonable to run the tests on dedicated capacity or will hosted API be able to sustain our throughput estimates? Also would you be able to include model variant comparisons (quantized vs fp16) and a baseline run against CloudCorp?

Thanks — Sam
Samantha Chen
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Analytics
Samantha.Chen@acmeanalytics.com

---
Attachment: sample-goldset.csv (stub)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Chen <samantha@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood competitive eval - post-call recap and ask

Hi Sam / Tom — really appreciate the clear list. High level: yes, we can run a focused bake-off that compares Redwood hosted + Dedicated capacity against your CloudCorp baseline. We’ll include model variant runs (fp16, int8 quant) and the cost/latency breakdown per model.

Attached is our proposed bake-off plan (redwood_bakeoff_plan_v1.pdf) with owners, timelines, and success criteria. Quick highlights:
- Owner: Aditya (sales lead) + Marissa (eng/ops lead) + Vivek (tech lead)
- Window: prefer 2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-13 (10 business days) — flexible if you need earlier start.
- Success criteria: p95 latency <= CloudCorp p95 * 1.2 (to allow for config differences), cost per 1M tokens <= CloudCorp cost * 0.85, and no more than 10% quality regression on the goldset (we’ll compute BLEU/ROUGE + human sample checks).
- Deliverables: test harness (JMeter + python runner), per-route dashboards, and raw logs for your team.

Action items for us (internal + for Acme):
A) Acme: share goldset + representative traffic profile + CloudCorp access tokens (Tom)
B) Redwood: build and share runner + run initial baseline on our side (Marissa/Vivek)
C) Kickoff sync: Tue 2026-03-02 10:00 PT (proposed)

Let us know if this aligns and if the success thresholds need tuning. We’ll also add a fallback plan to run larger batch sizes on Dedicated if hosted API hits rate limits.

Best,
Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

---

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: bake-off tasks and timeline (Acme)

Team — looping you in to own the technical deliverables for the Acme bake-off. Summary of assignments: 

- Vivek: set up test harness (JMeter + python runner), define the metrics to capture (p50/p95 latency, tokens, cost estimates, 99-99.9% tails for infra weirdness). Prepare scripts to run fp16 vs int8/shaved quant runs. Owner to validate run reproducibility.
- Lauren: prepare the infra — sandbox Dedicated pool sizing (4x A100 equiv) and hosted API rate limits, configure dashboards and retention, set up storage for logs.
- Marissa (me): oversee baseline runs, schedule kickoff, and coordinate access tokens with Acme. I’ll also own the initial analysis and the per-route reporting that we’ll share.

Timeline: 
- 2/26: test harness baseline smoke run with Redwood public models
- 3/2: kickoff w/ Acme, sync on dataset and tokens
- 3/3–3/12: bake-off executions
- 3/13: initial results and presentation to Acme

Please flag any capacity conflicts. Vivek — I included a short checklist in the attached test_cases.csv.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood competitive eval - technical plan and data request

Hi Sam / Tom — quick technical note ahead of the kickoff. A few asks to make the bake-off apples-to-apples: 

1) Dataset + tokens: please share the representative traffic profile (CSV preferred) and a sample of your goldset (we have your sample-goldset.csv already — thanks). The traffic profile should include request size distribution and expected concurrency.
2) CloudCorp baseline: we need the endpoints you currently hit (URL + expected model name/config) and a short note on batching/beam settings you use. If you can provide a single CloudCorp run logfile (or summary metrics), that would speed comparison.
3) Success check details: for quality we’ll compute automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity where applicable) and then select 20 human-eval samples for blind review by Acme. If you have any proprietary evaluation rubric, send it along.

Implementation notes: we’ll run the same request schedule against Redwood hosted API first (to measure noise and rate limits) and then move to a Dedicated pool sized to match target throughput. Expect the fp16 runs to be closest parity; int8 may show small quality drift. We’ll capture cost as total token compute + estimated infra amortized over the run.

Can you confirm you’ll share the CloudCorp token by EOD Mon 3/1? Also: can we lock the kickoff for Tue 3/2 10:00 PT? I’ll post the meeting invite once confirmed.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Thanks Vivek — we’ll share the CloudCorp token and a representative traffic CSV by EOD Mon 2026-03-01. Kickoff time Tue 3/2 10:00 PT works for us.

We appreciate the clear success criteria. A couple small asks from Acme: please include (a) a raw per-request latency histogram, and (b) an exported CSV of model outputs aligned to our goldset so we can run our own QA scripts. Otherwise go ahead and post the invite.

See you Tue — Sam
